places.name: Rottnest Island
places.ai_summary: Rottnest Island is a picturesque island near Perth, famous for its stunning beaches, crystal-clear waters, and the adorable quokkas. It's a popular destination for day trips and outdoor activities.
places.place_tip: Rent a bike to explore the island at your own pace.
places.address: Rottnest Island, Western Australia, Australia

places.name: Margaret River Wine Region
places.ai_summary: The Margaret River Wine Region is renowned for its premium wineries, gourmet food, and stunning coastal scenery. It's a must-visit destination for wine enthusiasts and food lovers.
places.place_tip: Join a guided wine tour to discover the best wineries in the region.
places.address: Margaret River, Western Australia, Australia

places.name: Kings Park and Botanic Garden (Perth)
places.ai_summary: Kings Park and Botanic Garden is one of the world's largest and most beautiful inner-city parks, offering stunning views of the Perth skyline and the Swan River. It's a perfect spot for picnics, walks, and enjoying nature.
places.place_tip: Don't miss the Lotterywest Federation Walkway for a treetop view.
places.address: Fraser Avenue, Perth WA 6005, Australia

places.name: Ningaloo Reef Marine Park
places.ai_summary: Ningaloo Reef Marine Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site, known for its stunning coral reef and diverse marine life. It's an excellent destination for snorkeling, diving, and whale shark swimming.
places.place_tip: Book a tour to swim with whale sharks for a memorable experience.
places.address: Ningaloo Reef Marine Park, Exmouth WA 6707, Australia

places.name: The Pinnacles Desert
places.ai_summary: The Pinnacles Desert is a unique landscape within Nambung National Park, featuring thousands of limestone pillars. It's a fascinating place to explore, with walking trails and a scenic drive.
places.place_tip: Take the time to walk among the Pinnacles for a closer look.
places.address: Nambung National Park, Cervantes WA 6511, Australia

places.name: Cable Beach (Broome)
places.ai_summary: Cable Beach is a famous beach in Broome, known for its stunning sunsets, white sand, and crystal-clear waters. It's a popular spot for swimming, sunbathing, and camel rides.

opening_hours.notes: Camel rides are available at specific times.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a camel ride along the beach at sunset for a memorable experience.
places.address: Cable Beach, Broome WA 6725, Australia

attribution.title: Cable Beach, Broome
attribution.author: Zoharby
attribution.description: Cable Beach, Broome. Taken Before sunset.

places.name: Karijini National Park
places.ai_summary: Karijini National Park is a stunning natural area in the Pilbara region, known for its dramatic gorges, waterfalls, and unique rock formations. It's a paradise for hikers and nature lovers.
places.place_tip: Take plenty of water and explore the many walking trails.
places.address: Karijini National Park, Tom Price WA 6751, Australia

attribution.title: Dales Gorge, WA
attribution.author: Graeme Churchard from Bristol (51.4414, -2.5242), UK

places.name: Fremantle
places.ai_summary: Fremantle is a vibrant, historic area known for its well-preserved 19th-century architecture, bustling markets, and lively arts scene. It's a great place to explore on foot.

opening_hours.notes: Some attractions may have extended hours.

places.place_tip: Visit the Fremantle Markets for local produce and crafts.
places.address: Fremantle, Western Australia, Australia

places.name: Horizontal Falls
places.ai_summary: Horizontal Falls, located in the Kimberley region, is a natural phenomenon where tidal waters rush through narrow gorges, creating a waterfall effect. It's best experienced by boat or seaplane.

opening_hours.notes: Access is tidal and weather dependent.

places.place_tip: Check the tide times and book a tour for the best experience.
places.address: Horizontal Falls, Western Australia, Australia

places.name: Bungle Bungle Range (Purnululu National Park)
places.ai_summary: The Bungle Bungles are a unique sandstone formation in Purnululu National Park, known for their beehive-shaped domes. The area is rich in Aboriginal culture and offers stunning hiking trails.

opening_hours.notes: Access is via guided tours only.

places.place_tip: Take a guided tour to learn about the geology and Aboriginal culture.
places.address: Purnululu National Park, Western Australia, Australia

attribution.title: Echidna chasm WA

places.name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
places.ai_summary: The Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk is a suspended walkway in the treetops of the ancient tingle forest, offering a unique perspective of the forest ecosystem. It's an easy walk suitable for all ages.
places.name_english: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
places.place_tip: Visit the Ancient Empire walk for a close-up view of the giant tingle trees.
places.address: Valley of the Giants, Denmark WA 6333, Australia

places.name: Wave Rock
places.ai_summary: Wave Rock is a natural rock formation that resembles a giant wave, located in Hyden. It's a popular stop for tourists, with walking trails and a nearby wildlife park.
places.place_tip: Explore the nearby Hyden Wildlife Park to see native animals.
places.address: Wave Rock, Hyden WA 6359, Australia

places.name: Swan River (Perth)
places.ai_summary: The Swan River is an iconic river in Western Australia, flowing through the heart of Perth. It's popular for boating, fishing, and riverside walks.

opening_hours.notes: Best viewed from the many parks and walkways along the river.

places.place_tip: Take a river cruise for a different perspective of the city.
places.address: Swan River, Perth WA 6004, Australia

places.name: Esperance
places.ai_summary: Esperance is a coastal town known for its stunning beaches, clear waters, and the nearby Cape Le Grand National Park. It's a great destination for relaxation and outdoor activities.

opening_hours.notes: Best enjoyed at a leisurely pace.

places.place_tip: Visit the nearby Cape Le Grand National Park for stunning coastal scenery.
places.address: Esperance, Western Australia, Australia

places.name: Cape Le Grand National Park
places.ai_summary: Cape Le Grand National Park is a stunning coastal park known for its white sand beaches, crystal-clear waters, and granite peaks. It's a paradise for nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts.
places.place_tip: Explore the many walking trails and enjoy the stunning beaches.
places.address: Cape Le Grand National Park, Esperance WA 6450, Australia

places.name: Monkey Mia (Dolphin feeding)
places.ai_summary: Monkey Mia is famous for its friendly wild dolphins that visit the beach daily. It's a unique opportunity to see these amazing creatures up close in their natural habitat.
places.place_tip: Observe the dolphins from the beach and follow the guidelines for a safe interaction.
places.address: Monkey Mia, Shark Bay WA 6537, Australia

places.name: Kalbarri National Park
places.ai_summary: Kalbarri National Park is known for its stunning river gorge, coastal cliffs, and diverse wildlife. It's a great destination for hiking, birdwatching, and enjoying the natural beauty of Western Australia.
places.place_tip: Visit the Z Bend and Nature's Window for stunning views.
places.address: Kalbarri National Park, Kalbarri WA 6536, Australia

places.name: Perth Mint
places.ai_summary: The Perth Mint is an iconic Australian attraction, known for its gold bullion and historic significance. Visitors can explore the mint's museum, see gold pouring demonstrations, and learn about the history of gold in Australia.
places.place_tip: Don't miss the gold pouring demonstration.
places.address: Perth Mint, 310 Hay St, East Perth WA 6004, Australia

places.name: Cottesloe Beach
places.ai_summary: Cottesloe Beach is one of Perth's most iconic beaches, known for its clear waters, white sand, and vibrant sunset views. It's a popular spot for swimming, picnicking, and enjoying the beach lifestyle.

opening_hours.notes: Best enjoyed at a leisurely pace.

places.place_tip: Visit the nearby Cottesloe Hotel for a drink with a view.
places.address: Cottesloe Beach, Cottesloe WA 6011, Australia

places.name: Bell Tower (Perth)
places.ai_summary: The Bell Tower is a historic landmark in Perth, known for its distinctive architecture and the twelve bells that were gifted by the Queen. Visitors can enjoy panoramic views of the city and the Swan River from the tower.
places.place_tip: Visit during the day for a guided tour and enjoy the views.
places.address: Bell Tower, Barrack Square, Perth WA 6000, Australia
